params.body:
A second pass on the top dropdown. The previous one went from 12px corners with a solid blue block to 6px with a marker; this goes the rest of the way.

Round corners on a panel that hangs off a straight bar make it float, and a rounded block inside a margin turns a menu line into a little button. The house guide asks for text that behaves, not pills.

So: no corners, no inner padding, rows edge to edge. The highlight becomes a band across the full width, which is what a menu line is.

## And a real defect alongside it

Hover was blue at 9% and "you are here" blue at 12%. Those are not separable by eye: under the cursor every item read as the current one, and only the 2px marker still carried the difference — on a screenshot with the mouse over *Werking*, both rows looked selected.

Hover is now grey (`#f2f4f7`, ink-coloured text). Grey says "the mouse is here", blue says "you are here".

## What changed

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| panel corners | 6px | 0 |
| panel padding | 5px | 0 |
| row corners | 4px | 0 |
| row padding | 7px 11px | 8px 14px |
| gap between rows | 2px | 0, bands touch |
| active marker | 2px, inset 5px top and bottom | 3px, full height, flush left |
| hover | blue 9% | grey |

The gap between rows existed because rounded blocks stuck to their neighbour and read as one continuous smear. With straight edges touching is the point, so it goes.

`overflow: hidden` on the panel, so a full-bleed band cannot sit outside the border.

## Verified

CSS only, no markup and no rule change (styling changes nothing in the rule catalogue). `npm run build` green — lightningcss parses and minifies it, which is what rejects a broken selector. `StylesheetSyntaxTest` green.
params.title: A menu is not a card: square panel, full-bleed rows
